questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a main factor that drives the design of software products?
options: Needs not met by current products
The desire to use a specific programming language
Changes in technology making new products possible
questions.correctAnswer: The desire to use a specific programming language
questions.explanation: Product design is driven by unmet consumer needs, dissatisfaction with existing software, and technological changes—not a developer's desire to use a particular programming language.

questions.question: A fragment of functionality in a system, such as a 'print' option, is called a:
questions.explanation: A feature is a coherent fragment of functionality offered by a software system, such as a 'print' or 'change background' capability.

questions.question: Which user understanding technique is described as inexpensive and highly valuable for small companies?
questions.explanation: Informal user analysis and discussions with potential users are inexpensive and practical ways for small companies to understand user needs.

questions.question: 'Imagined users' created as character portraits to help understand product needs are known as:
questions.explanation: Personas are imagined character portraits representing typical target users of a product.

questions.question: Which aspect of a persona description details the individual's level of technical skills?
questions.explanation: The education element of a persona covers both educational background and level of technical skill and competence.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of using personas?
options: They provide exact statistical data on market size.
They help developers empathize with potential users.
They dictate the underlying database architecture.
questions.correctAnswer: They help developers empathize with potential users.
questions.explanation: Personas help developers step into the shoes of target users and empathize with their goals and skills rather than designing for themselves.

questions.question: A persona developed quickly on the basis of limited user information is called a:
questions.explanation: A proto-persona is a lightweight persona created rapidly from existing team knowledge when time or budget does not allow extensive user research.

questions.question: A narrative that describes how a user or group might use a system to achieve an objective is a:
questions.explanation: A scenario is a structured narrative describing a realistic situation in which a user or group interacts with the product to accomplish a goal.

questions.question: Which of the following is an essential element of a scenario description?
options: An explanation of problems that can't be addressed by the existing system
The specific programming language to be used
questions.correctAnswer: An explanation of problems that can't be addressed by the existing system
questions.explanation: A scenario description includes the scenario name, overall objective, personas involved, activities, problems that cannot be addressed by the existing system, and proposed solutions.

questions.question: Scenarios should always be written from whose perspective?
questions.explanation: Scenarios must always be written from the user's perspective, describing their goals and actions rather than internal system mechanics.

questions.question: According to the slides, what is a common problem when real users try to write scenarios?
options: They invent too many new features.
They focus too much on how they work currently and write too much detail.
They only write user stories instead.
questions.correctAnswer: They focus too much on how they work currently and write too much detail.
questions.explanation: Real users often focus heavily on their current workflows and include excessive operational detail instead of envisioning new ways of working.

questions.question: What is the standard format for a user story?
options: I want to <do something> as a <role>.
As a <role>, I <want | need> to <do something> so that <reason>.
questions.correctAnswer: As a <role>, I <want | need> to <do something> so that <reason>.
questions.explanation: The standard user story template is "As a <role>, I <want | need> to <do something> [so that <reason>]."

questions.question: A complex feature that will take several sprints to implement and must be broken down is called an:
questions.explanation: An epic is a large, coarse-grained user story or complex feature that spans multiple sprints and is decomposed into smaller stories.

questions.question: Why are scenarios often considered more natural than user stories for interacting with real users?
options: They read naturally and provide context about normal ways of working.
They translate directly into Python code.
questions.correctAnswer: They read naturally and provide context about normal ways of working.
questions.explanation: Scenarios read like natural narratives and provide rich context about how users normally work, making them easier for users to relate to than isolated user stories.

questions.question: If a feature is linked to a single item of functionality and has no side-effects, it possesses which characteristic?
questions.explanation: A coherent feature does one clear thing and avoids unexpected side effects.

questions.question: Which type of knowledge helps you think of new, innovative ways of helping users by understanding the work area (e.g., finance)?
questions.explanation: Domain knowledge is understanding the specific application or business area (such as finance or healthcare), enabling innovative ways to support work in that area.

questions.question: To encourage users to adopt your system, you must find a balance between novel features and:
questions.explanation: Feature design involves balancing familiarity (so users feel comfortable adopting the product) with novelty (so the product offers new value).

questions.question: The trade-off between having the software do things for the user versus allowing the user to configure the system is called:
questions.explanation: Automation vs Control is the trade-off between automating actions on the user's behalf and giving users explicit control and configuration options.

questions.question: What term describes the negative consequence of adding too many new features in response to user requests?
questions.explanation: Feature creep (or feature bloat) occurs when excessive features are continuously added, making the product complex, harder to use, and harder to maintain.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common reason why feature creep occurs?
options: Developers refuse to write new code.
Developers try to match all features found in competing products.
The system relies on open-source libraries.
questions.correctAnswer: Developers try to match all features found in competing products.
questions.explanation: Feature creep commonly happens when product teams reluctance to say 'no' to user requests or try to match every feature offered by competing products.
